close_reason: Decided yes (Mark 2026-05-13) — ship Multipurpose Profile types as siblings to the Strict tier types, after the Strict surface is complete. Rationale: AGENTS.md prelaunch framing (design for eventual complete shape; no-consumer-asking is not informative); PKIX-mzsk spec-taxonomy principle names all BR cells as in-scope; PKIX-e3nl temporal-posture principle is neutral on this (Multipurpose is parallel current-tier, not historical). Surface cost is bounded: 8 new public identifiers in pkix-profiles-cabf (4 types + 4 fns), 0 new crates, ~4 new test fixtures, 0 new pkix-chain wrappers (use-case wrappers are Profile-parameterized already). Implementation plan filed as PKIX-jbvb.9 epic with 5 children (1 rename + 4 Multipurpose tiers).
description:
## What

After PKIX-jbvb.7 lands, `pkix-profiles-cabf` will ship one canonical Profile
type per S/MIME validation tier (Mailbox / Sponsor / Individual / [pending
PKIX-jbvb.1] Organization), each targeting the Strict generation. This bead
captures the open architectural question: should the crate eventually ship
**multi-generation** Profile types, e.g. `SmimeSponsorValidatedMultipurpose`
alongside `SmimeSponsorValidated` (Strict)?

## Context

S/MIME BR §7.1.6.1 names 12 distinct subscriber-cert profile cells:
4 validation tiers × 3 generations (Legacy / Multipurpose / Strict), each
with its own reserved policy OID:

| Validation type | Legacy `.1` | Multipurpose `.2` | Strict `.3` |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mailbox-validated | `2.23.140.1.5.1.1` (banned) | `.1.2` | `.1.3` |
| Organization-validated | `.2.1` (banned) | `.2.2` | `.2.3` |
| Sponsor-validated | `.3.1` (banned) | `.3.2` | `.3.3` |
| Individual-validated | `.4.1` (banned) | `.4.2` | `.4.3` |

Legacy is banned for new issuance per §7.1.6.1 line 2600 (effective
2025-07-15). Remaining modern surface: 4 × 2 = 8 cells.

Mark's 2026-05-13 decision (PKIX-jbvb.6) picked the **one-Profile-per-
validation-type, Strict-targeted** shape for now. PKIX-jbvb.7 implements that.

## The open question

Should the eventual complete shape ship 8 Profile types (Strict + Multipurpose
× 4 tiers) or stay at 4 (one per tier, Strict only)?

### Arguments for staying at 4 (status quo after PKIX-jbvb.7)

- The spec-taxonomy principle (PKIX-mzsk) lists *validation-type* variants
  (Mailbox/Org/Sponsor/Individual) as in-scope, not generation variants.
- Strict is the BR's stated "long term target profile" (glossary §372);
  Multipurpose is a transitional bridge for document-signing crossover.
- Each generation primarily differs in EKU permissiveness (line 2053-2054:
  Strict requires emailProtection-only; Multipurpose/Legacy allow others).
  The current `ValidationPolicy` shape doesn't have an "EKU is exactly
  this set" predicate, so multi-generation Profile types would currently
  produce nearly-identical `ValidationPolicy` outputs differing only in
  policy-OID assertion.
- Maintenance cost: doubles the type surface; each BR refresh has to
  audit 8 Profile types instead of 4.

### Arguments for shipping 8

- BR §7.1.6.1 explicitly names all 12 cells; each has its own OID. By
  strict reading of "ships Profile types for each subscriber-cert profile
  named in the BR," that's the target.
- Prelaunch framing (AGENTS.md): "design for the eventual complete shape,"
  "breaking changes are free." Pre-1.0 is when surface expansion is
  cheapest.
- `pkix-policy-zlint`'s comprehensive-coverage role is *predicate*
  coverage, not *taxonomy* coverage. The `-cabf` crate is supposed to own
  the taxonomy axis.
- Multipurpose certs exist in the field (document-signing crossover).
  Validators may need to assert "this cert is conforming Multipurpose
  Individual-validated" distinctly from Strict.

### Hybrid options

- (a) Ship 4 now, file 4 follow-up beads for Multipurpose Profile types,
  prioritize based on demand signals when they surface.
- (b) Ship 8 now under the prelaunch "design for eventual complete shape"
  framing. Pre-1.0 surface expansion is cheap.
- (c) Add a `Generation` enum parameter to each Profile type, so one
  `SmimeSponsorValidated` carries `(Generation::Strict | Generation::Multipurpose)`.
  Avoids doubling the type count; trades for a different ergonomic surface.
- (d) Stay at 4 forever (Strict-only); document that Multipurpose cert
  validation requires hand-construction of `ValidationPolicy` or use of
  `pkix-policy-zlint`.

## Filing rationale

This decision touches the spec-taxonomy principle in AGENTS.md and is
post-PKIX-jbvb.7 architectural shape. Defer until at least one of:

1. PKIX-jbvb.1 (Organization-validated) ships — gives us 4 complete
   tier types to evaluate the "4 vs 8" question against concrete code.
2. A concrete consumer ask surfaces for Multipurpose distinction.
3. A separate review sweep flags the gap.

Marking `human` to keep it out of the autonomous ready queue.

## Cross-references

- PKIX-jbvb.6 (decision on Strict vs Multipurpose for Sponsor/Individual)
- PKIX-jbvb.7 (implementation of the Strict-only shape)
- PKIX-mzsk (AGENTS.md spec-taxonomy principle)
- AGENTS.md "Project phase and decision framing" section
- specs/cabforum-smime-BR.md §7.1.6.1
title: pkix-profiles-cabf: decide whether to ship multi-generation Profile types (Strict + Multipurpose × 4 validation tiers)
